chunks: Tawhid al-Saduq: From Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdallah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Exempted from my Umma are nine things: error, forgetfulness, what they are coerced to do, what they do not have the strength for, what they do not know, what they have to do out of necessity, jealousy, bad omen, and thinking about the whispered (Shaytan-inspired) prompts in regards the creation – so long as it is not voiced aloud.

key_terms.الوسوسة: Whispered prompts or doubts (often from Shaytan)

ai.seo_question: What are the nine things from which the Umma is exempted according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Shaykh al-Saduq, outlines nine specific exemptions from divine accountability (hukm) for the Umma, emphasizing the mercy inherent in Islamic jurisprudence. It distinguishes between external factors like coercion and necessity, and internal states such as forgetfulness and unvoiced doubts (waswasa), establishing a nuanced framework for moral responsibility. This enumeration is foundational in Shia legal theory for determining when a sin is incurred versus when it is excused.
